checks.claim: In a car engine, burning fuel and air pushes a piston down inside a cylinder.
checks.why: Haynes and RepairPal: the spark ignites the compressed fuel-air mix and the expanding gas forces the piston down (the power stroke).

sources.title: How a car engine works - Haynes
How Does Your Engine Work? - RepairPal

checks.claim: A connecting rod and crankshaft turn the piston's up-and-down motion into rotation.
checks.why: The connecting rod links piston and crank pin; together they convert reciprocating motion into rotation.

sources.title: Crankshafts convert vertical movement of pistons into a rotation

checks.claim: Intake valves let the fuel and air in and exhaust valves let the burnt gases out.
checks.why: Four-stroke cycle: the intake valve opens on the intake stroke, the exhaust valve opens so the rising piston pushes the burnt gases out.

sources.title: The Four Stroke Engine Cycle - AeroToolbox

checks.claim: A water pump circulates coolant around the cylinders to keep the engine from overheating.
checks.why: The pump pushes coolant through the block and head passages around the cylinders, then to the radiator; without it the engine overheats.

sources.title: Cooling System Basics - O'Reilly Auto Parts
